reason: The text explicitly portrays the Hebrews (Israelites/the people - הָעָם) as followers of Yahweh (יְהוָה). Throughout this passage from Exodus 19, Yahweh directly communicates commands to Moses for the people, directs their preparation and sanctification, and is preparing to reveal himself to them at Mount Sinai. The people are portrayed as obedient to Yahweh's instructions, following his requirements regarding the sacred mountain, and preparing themselves as his covenant people. The entire passage centers on the Hebrew people's relationship of subordination and reverence toward Yahweh as their God.
